claim: A defendant raising an ineffective assistance of counsel claim on direct appeal must make specific allegations of the conduct that constitutes deficient performance only when the alleged deficiency involves the failure to file pretrial motions, but not when the alleged deficiency concerns voir dire conduct.
initial_reasoning: The reported decision at 984 N.W.2d 261 does not contain language establishing a rule that a defendant must allege specific deficient conduct only when the alleged failure involves filing pre‑trial motions and not when it concerns voir‑dire conduct. The case discusses ineffective assistance standards generally, but it does not draw the precise distinction asserted in the claim.
